name: Frail Elderly (FE) Waiver
summary: The Frail Elderly Waiver is a KanCare (Kansas Medicaid) program that pays for in-home help for people 65 and older who would otherwise need a nursing home. Members can self-direct personal care and hire a relative, including a spouse. A Financial Management Services agency handles payroll and taxes.
who_qualifies: Meets the nursing-facility level of care on the functional assessment done through the Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC).
A waiver slot is available (new applicants have been placed on a waitlist since July 6, 2026).

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — adult children and other relatives can be hired for self-directed personal care.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: yes — a spouse can be hired as the self-directed attendant.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: n/a — the FE waiver serves people 65 and older.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the worker may live with the member or not.

pay.detail: KDADS sets personal care rates; KMAP posted SFY 2025 FE personal care rates of $6.83–$7.50 per 15 minutes (paid to the provider or FMS). Self-directed worker wages are reported at about $13–$17 an hour; the worker's wage is set with the member inside the plan.

hours_or_budget: The ADRC functional assessment and the KanCare plan care coordinator set the personal care hours in the person-centered service plan.

waitlist.detail: KDADS started a waitlist for new FE applicants on July 6, 2026 because funding did not cover demand; people already in process continue and emergency exceptions exist.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Members can use an agency or self-direct (hire, train, fire) with a Financial Management Services agency doing payroll and taxes.
how_to_apply: Apply for KanCare online, by phone at 800-792-4884, or on paper, and check the box for HCBS services.
Call the ADRC at 855-200-2372 to schedule the functional assessment.
If found eligible, you may be placed on the FE waitlist until a slot opens.
When enrolled, choose self-direction and an FMS provider through your KanCare plan, then hire your relative.

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my wife or husband in Kansas?
faqs.a: Yes. On the FE waiver, a spouse can be hired as the self-directed attendant.

faqs.q: Is there a waiting list for the Frail Elderly waiver?
faqs.a: Yes, since July 6, 2026 for new applicants. People already being processed continue, and emergencies can be considered.
The Financial Management Services agency runs payroll, withholds taxes and pays the worker. The member is still the boss.

faqs.q: How much do self-directed workers earn?
faqs.a: Reported wages are about $13 to $17 an hour. KDADS sets the service rate and the FMS pays the worker.
The Aging and Disability Resource Center, at 855-200-2372.

name: Physical Disability (PD) Waiver
summary: The Physical Disability Waiver is a KanCare program for people ages 16 to 64 with physical disabilities who need a nursing-facility level of care. Members can self-direct personal care and hire a family member. Kansas lets spouses and parents of minors be paid personal care workers on this waiver if they meet provider rules.
who_qualifies: Kansas resident ages 16 to 64 with a physical disability (Social Security disability determination or equivalent).
Meets nursing-facility level of care on the ADRC functional assessment.
Financially eligible for KanCare (for minors, only the youth's income counts).

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — relatives can be hired as self-directed personal care workers.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: yes — spouses may be paid for personal care if they meet provider qualifications.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — parents of members under 18 may be paid for personal care if they meet provider qualifications.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the worker may live with the member or not.

pay.detail: KMAP's SFY 2025 PD personal care rates were $4.10–$4.88 per 15 minutes depending on modifier (about $16–$20 an hour paid to the provider or FMS); SFY 2026 brought further increases. Self-directed worker wages are reported at about $13–$17 an hour.

hours_or_budget: Hours come from the ADRC assessment and the person-centered service plan built with the KanCare plan.

waitlist.detail: Kansas eliminated the PD waitlist at the end of FY2025; some sources still report a list, so ask the ADRC about current status.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Self-direction uses a Financial Management Services agency for payroll and taxes; agency-directed care is also available.
how_to_apply: Apply for KanCare (800-792-4884 or online), checking the HCBS box.
Contact the ADRC (855-200-2372) for the functional assessment.
After enrollment, choose self-direction and an FMS agency, then hire your relative.

faqs.q: Can a parent be paid to care for a teen on the PD waiver?
faqs.a: Yes. Kansas allows parents of minors to be paid for personal care on the PD waiver if they meet provider qualifications.

faqs.q: What ages does the PD waiver serve?
faqs.a: Ages 16 to 64. People who turn 65 can move to the Frail Elderly waiver.

faqs.q: Is there a waitlist for the PD waiver?
faqs.a: Kansas eliminated the PD waitlist at the end of fiscal year 2025. Check with the ADRC for current status.

faqs.q: Can I be paid to care for my disabled spouse in Kansas?
faqs.a: Yes, on the PD waiver a spouse can be the paid personal care worker.

name: Brain Injury (BI) Waiver
summary: The Brain Injury Waiver is a KanCare program for children and adults with an acquired or traumatic brain injury who would otherwise need institutional care. It covers personal care plus therapies and skill-building services. Personal care can be self-directed, and Kansas allows spouses and parents of minors to be paid personal care workers.
who_qualifies: Kansas resident with a qualifying brain injury, birth to age 64.
Meets the required level of care on the functional assessment.
Financially eligible for KanCare (for children, only the child's income counts).

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — relatives can be hired as personal care workers.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: yes — spouses may be paid for personal care if they meet provider qualifications.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — parents of minors may be paid for personal care if they meet provider qualifications.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the worker may live with the member or not.

pay.detail: KDADS sets BI personal care rates (raised for SFY 2026 per KMAP Bulletin 25122). Self-directed worker wages are reported at about $13–$17 an hour.

hours_or_budget: Personal care hours are set in the person-centered service plan after the functional assessment.

waitlist.detail: No BI waitlist is published, but reporting after 2025 budget cuts said BI could see its first-ever waitlist.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Self-directed care uses a Financial Management Services agency; agency-directed care is also available.
how_to_apply: Apply for KanCare (800-792-4884 or online), checking the HCBS box.
Contact the ADRC (855-200-2372) to request the BI functional assessment.
Once enrolled, choose self-direction and an FMS agency, then hire your relative.

faqs.q: Can I be paid to care for my son with a brain injury in Kansas?
faqs.a: Yes. Kansas allows parents, including parents of minors, to be paid personal care workers on the BI waiver.

faqs.q: Does the BI waiver have a waiting list?
faqs.a: None is published now, but budget cuts in 2025 raised the risk of a first-time waitlist. Apply early.

faqs.q: What services does the BI waiver cover?
faqs.a: Personal care, therapies, cognitive rehabilitation, transitional living skills, home changes, meals and more.

faqs.q: Can a spouse be paid on the BI waiver?
faqs.a: Yes, if the spouse meets provider qualifications.

faqs.q: Who handles my relative's paycheck if we self-direct?
faqs.a: A Financial Management Services agency runs payroll and taxes. The member, or a chosen representative, still hires and supervises the worker.

name: Technology Assisted (TA) Waiver
summary: The Technology Assisted Waiver is a KanCare program for medically fragile children and young adults up to age 21 who rely on technology such as a ventilator, trach or feeding tube. Parents' income is not counted. Parents can be paid for personal care up to 12 hours a day, and parents who are RNs or LPNs can be paid for nursing.
who_qualifies: Kansas resident from birth to age 21.
Depends on medical technology and needs a hospital level of care.
Financially eligible based on the child's own income; parents' income is not counted.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — other relatives can be hired as personal care workers.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: n/a — the TA waiver serves children and young adults.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — parents can be paid for up to 12 hours a day of personal care (40 hours a week max, no overnight respite); RN/LPN parents may also provide up to 8 hours a day of nursing.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — not required by published rules, though most paid parents live with the child.

pay.detail: KDADS sets TA personal care and nursing rates (raised for SFY 2026 per KMAP Bulletin 25122). Self-directed personal care wages are reported at about $13–$17 an hour.

hours_or_budget: The assessment and plan of care set daily personal care and nursing hours; paid-parent hours are capped as above.

waitlist.detail: A 2026 KDADS amendment proposed adding a TA waitlist (proposed effective May 1, 2026) along with updated legally-responsible-individual rules; CMS approval was not confirmed.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Personal care can be self-directed with a Financial Management Services agency or agency-delivered.
how_to_apply: Contact the TA waiver assessor, Family Waiver Care, at 785-296-9551.
Apply for KanCare for the child (800-792-4884), checking the HCBS box.
After approval, choose self-direction and an FMS agency, and enroll the parent as the personal care worker.

faqs.q: Can parents get paid to care for a medically fragile child in Kansas?
faqs.a: Yes. On the TA waiver, parents can be paid for up to 12 hours a day of personal care, capped at 40 hours a week.

faqs.q: Can a nurse parent be paid for nursing?
faqs.a: Yes. Parents who are RNs or LPNs can provide up to 8 hours a day of nursing.
No. Only the child's income counts for TA waiver eligibility.

faqs.q: Is there a waitlist for the TA waiver?
faqs.a: Historically no. A 2026 amendment proposed adding one, so ask the assessor about current status.
The TA waiver serves birth to 21. Older youth may move to the PD or BI waiver.
